findings.title: [P1] Pass branch names as argv instead of shell text
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell metacharacters, `exec(\`git show ${branch}\`)` interprets them as commands. For example, `HEAD; id` runs `id` with the application's privileges. It also changes process lifecycle and cancellation semantics because the returned process represents a shell rather than Git. Preserve argument separation with `execFile` or an equivalent non-shell API.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the branch as a single argument to keep Git’s lifecycle intact
findings.body:
A legal Git branch such as `topic&false` is interpreted by the shell as backgrounded `git show topic` followed by `false`. The returned process therefore tracks the shell rather than Git, can exit before Git finishes, and `.kill()` targets the shell while Git may continue running.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass branch names as argv instead of shell text
findings.body:
`exec` interpolates `branch` into a shell command, enabling arbitrary command execution with process privileges. On POSIX, the valid branch input `HEAD;id` runs `git show HEAD` followed by `id`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch through `execFile` instead of a shell
findings.body:
`branch` is interpolated into a shell command, enabling arbitrary command execution when it contains shell metacharacters. For example, `showBranch("main; touch /tmp/pwned")` executes both commands under the application’s privileges. This affects any caller passing untrusted or insufficiently validated branch input.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
